history.summary: IDENTITY FLAG: No independently documented 'Laxman Shrine' exists at Deshnoke in any web source consulted. Laxman (Lakshman) is Karni Mata's stepson whose drowning at Kapil Sarovar (Kolayat tehsil) and Karni Mata's failed plea to Yama is the origin legend of the kabba rats at the Karni Mata Temple, Deshnoke - Yama relented and reincarnated Laxman and her male descendants as rats. The CSV row likely refers to a shrine within or associated with the Karni Mata Temple complex, or confuses the legend with a physical shrine; identity is ambiguous and should be verified on the ground. Coordinates given are those of the Karni Mata Temple itself (geocode FULL_ADDRESS match, relevance 93), as an approximate location only. The Karni Mata complex: innermost temple traditionally 15th century; present marble structure in late Mughal style completed early 20th century by Maharaja Ganga Singh of Bikaner; silver doors and marble facade his gift; further embellishment 1999 by jeweler Kundanlal Verma. Golden doors commissioned by Maharaja Bakhtawar Singh of Alwar.

town_description: Deshnoke is a small town about 30 km south of Bikaner in Bikaner district, Rajasthan. It is best known for the Karni Mata Temple - the famous 'Temple of Rats' - which draws both devotees of the Charan community and curious visitors from across the world. The town was traditionally founded in 1470.
